description: #222 (a) — m24's world with one file added: a 0-byte `.git/index.lock` is already sitting in the CALLER's worktree when the run starts. The merge runner does not read or write the caller's index, so there is nothing to stop for: both PRs merge, the integration verification is green and the status/stop_reason/targets are byte-for-byte m24's. What changes is that the report NAMES the lock — `caller_index_lock_pre_existing`, with the path, the size and the mtime — so the operator whose next `git pull --ff-only` dies on it can see that it predates this run rather than reading it as 'the merge broke' and rolling back merges that already landed. `caller_index_lock_appeared` must NOT be recorded: this one was not produced here. And the file is still on disk afterwards — the runner never removes another process's lock, because removing it corrupts the index it was protecting.
